Q: Open Claw- MS/Anthropic A:

The U.S. government ordered Anthropic not to allow anyone who's not a U.S. citizen to access the Mythos or Fable models - which includes some of Anthropic's employees. Since Anthropic is an American company they can use national security legislation to make the order.

In practice since they didn't immediately have the capability to distinguish which users are citizens and which aren't, they have turned off access for everyone for the moment. It's pretty much as simple as that.

https://www.anthropic.com/news/fable-mythos-access says

The US government, citing national security authorities, has issued an export control directive to suspend all access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 by any foreign national, whether inside or outside the United States, including foreign national Anthropic employees. The net effect of this order is that we must abruptly disable Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all our customers to ensure compliance. Access to all other Anthropic models will not be affected.

Q: How to stop relying on AI when writing code? A:

You can't go back, none of us can. Just like no one is writing machine code or no one uses text editors instead of IDE to code. It all depends on what coding means to you.

If you are coding to get a job or release an app you wont go back, you must ask yourself if you love programing or are you using it to for financial reasons.

For me it is both and when it is for money, I simply tell AI to do it and give me a complete app without me contributing anything.

When it is for pleasure though, since I am interested to learn the language (currently c#) I follow the tutorial do something daily with it because it feels good to discover something new.

so, if you are programing for both reasons, do what I did. If you don't enjoy it then let ai do it.

Q: Is getting the general structure of code from AI cheating? A:

Now my question is, if that is cheating?

Cheating who?

You are not cheating Neetcode. Neetcode is simply a tool for learning. But you may be cheating yourself out of the opportunity to learn how to write the code structure by over-using AI.

What you learn, how much you learn, and how you go about learning are all >your< business not ours. So make up your own mind if that is cheating.
